text.tspan: Normalised as score / Joint ceiling, the same scale the retention matrices use.
Backward transfer is final − just-learned. The random floor is not 0 on this scale; on Pong it is −100%.
Every number is computed over the tasks that run has finished, counted under each column. Nothing is
extrapolated, so the columns are not comparable. A mean over fewer tasks is not a mean over five.
The last task has nothing trained after it, so the row above it excludes it and measures retention alone.
* Forward transfer against from-scratch single-task runs on the same configuration. Averaged over
Breakout and Q*bert only, the games all three runs have a usable learning curve for. Ours logged no
curve for Space Invaders or Boxing, its run having resumed mid-sequence, and Pong is
ill-conditioned for every method because the baseline saturates before the window opens.
CLEAR logged no curves. Normalised by the from-scratch expert peak, as the definition
requires, not by the Joint ceiling the rows above use; the threshold scale in fwt.json is
more favourable to us and was not adopted.
